SD-senate.statusNote: Sen. Mike Rounds (R) won the June 2 primary with 75.8% and seeks a third term. Democratic nominee Julian Beaudion suspended his campaign Aug 4, leaving independent Brian Bengs, the 2022 Democratic Senate nominee, as Rounds's main challenger.

SD-governor.statusNote: Gov. Larry Rhoden (R), who succeeded Kristi Noem when she left to lead Homeland Security in January 2025, won the state's first-ever primary runoff July 28, 71% to 29% over Toby Doeden, after the June 2 field (Doeden 31%, Rhoden 25%, Rep. Dusty Johnson 23%, Speaker Jon Hansen 21%) missed the 35% threshold. He faces Democrat Dan Ahlers, and Dusty Johnson gave up his House seat to run.

SD-house-at-large.statusNote: General election field from South Dakota's June 2, 2026 primary: Marty Jackley (Republican), Nicole Gronli (Democrat). Open seat: Rep. Dusty Johnson ran for governor instead of re-election. No minor party or independent candidate is listed in either source. Both candidates fully researched Aug 17, 2026, but the race is held at names-only because the two overlap on only 6 of the 10 issues: Jackley has no documented position on health, housing, climate or education, so a match percentage would be built from different questions for each candidate.

sources.label: The Green Papers, South Dakota 2026 general election

SD-house-at-large.heldBack: Positions researched but held back: overlap 6 of 10, below the floor of 7.

candidates.name: Mike Rounds
candidates.background: U.S. Senator since 2015 and a former two-term governor of South Dakota (2003-2011); insurance and real estate businessman from Pierre. Won the June 2 Republican primary with 75.8% and is seeking a third term with President Trump's endorsement.
priorities: Permanent extension of the 2017 tax cuts

health.label: Would 'repeal and replace' Obamacare 'with market-based, patient-centered solutions'; adamantly opposes single-payer (Ballotpedia)

immigration.label: Voted for the reconciliation bill touting '$3.3 billion for Border Security' to support DHS border, immigration, and counterdrug enforcement (Senate office)

taxes.label: Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill's 'permanent extension of the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act', plus no tax on tips and overtime deductions (Senate office)

climate.label: Supports the Keystone Pipeline and 'all forms of domestic energy'; opposes higher taxes on energy producers (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Pledges to 'abolish the US Department of Education' in favor of local control (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Pro-life; as governor signed a 2006 bill banning most abortions (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: Cosponsored the Senate SAVE Act requiring proof of citizenship to register: 'making sure only United States citizens are voting... this rule has been loosely enforced in blue states for far too long' (rounds.senate.gov, Jan 16, 2026)

nullNotes.cost: checked Ballotpedia and his Senate office recap; tax provisions are scored under taxes, no distinct cost-of-living mechanism documented
nullNotes.housing: checked Ballotpedia and Senate office recap, nothing documented
nullNotes.safety: checked Ballotpedia and Senate office recap, nothing documented beyond routine appropriations

candidates.name: Brian Bengs
candidates.now: Retired Air Force officer and former Northern State University professor
candidates.background: Navy enlistee who became an Air Force JAG officer, retiring as a lieutenant colonel after 19 years, then taught criminal justice and government at Northern State University. The 2022 Democratic nominee against John Thune, he is running in 2026 as an independent, saying 'Big Money has so completely corrupted our political system.' Became Rounds's main challenger after Democrat Julian Beaudion suspended his campaign Aug 4.

cost.label: Fair wages, targeted subsidies, and tax credits so full-time workers can 'live with dignity' (campaign policy positions)

immigration.label: Supports 'increased legal immigration' with strong border security: 'immigration is crucial to American economic growth' (campaign policy positions)

taxes.label: 'Unrig the tax code' so the ultra-rich 'pay their fair share once again, like they had to in the 1960s', lowering taxes for small businesses and workers (campaign policy positions)

climate.label: Says maximizing clean energy development offers 'a unique two for one return on our investment'; backs clean-energy tax incentives and more renewable energy research funding (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Supports 'responsible investments in public education and job training programs' (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: 'I respect a woman's right to choose and support abortion restrictions after the point of viability with exceptions for the life or health of a mother' (campaign policy positions)

democracy.label: Backs protecting Native American voting rights and access to the ballot (campaign policy positions)

health.label: Defends Medicare against privatization ('so Big Money can further profit off the backs of senior citizens') and wants a full affordability overhaul of the system (Bengs campaign)

nullNotes.housing: campaign says homeownership is 'an unachievable dream' but documents no public-build or deregulation mechanism, so it does not map to the axis
nullNotes.safety: checked campaign policy positions and Ballotpedia, nothing documented

candidates.name: Larry Rhoden
candidates.background: Rancher, custom welder, and longtime legislator who became governor in January 2025 when Kristi Noem resigned to lead Homeland Security; he had been her lieutenant governor. Seeking a full term, he finished second June 2 (25% to Doeden's 31%) then won the state's first-ever runoff July 28 with 71%, carrying 64 of 66 counties.
priorities: Protect landowners from pipeline eminent domain

health.label: Pledged to work with President Trump to enforce Medicaid work requirements for expansion recipients (South Dakota Searchlight via Yahoo)

taxes.label: Proposed, shepherded, and signed a law designed to slow property tax increases within two months of taking office (South Dakota Searchlight)

education.label: Backed the $4 million education savings account program giving up to $3,000 per student in public funds for private school or homeschool (South Dakota Searchlight via Yahoo)

safety.label: Committed to building the new men's prison, an estimated $825 million project: 'This is the year to finish the job' (South Dakota Searchlight via Yahoo)

repro.label: Signed HB 1274 letting the attorney general prosecute abortion pill trafficking, plus fetal development curriculum mandates: 'South Dakota is the most pro-life state in America' (Live Action)

candidates.name: Dan Ahlers
candidates.now: Executive director of the South Dakota Democratic Party
candidates.background: Executive director of the South Dakota Democratic Party, a Dell Rapids small business owner of more than 20 years, and a former member of both the state House and Senate from District 25. Unopposed for the Democratic nomination, he argues 50 years of Republican governors 'proves it's time' for a change.
priorities: Wages that let South Dakotans get ahead
Keep rural hospitals and nursing homes open
Invest in teachers and school infrastructure

cost.label: 'Fight for wages that let hardworking South Dakotans get ahead, not just get by' (campaign issues)

health.label: 'Fight to keep rural hospitals open' and 'expand access to mental health services across the state' (campaign issues)

housing.label: Would leverage existing state programs and work with builders on affordable neighborhoods; cites builders unwilling to build under $600,000 and backs lower-cost methods like hempcrete (SDPB)

taxes.label: 'We have to find a better way to tax, a fair way to tax': wants tax equity across industries, noting banks pay franchise taxes while trusts go untaxed (SDPB)

education.label: 'Recruit and retain great teachers' and 'invest in school infrastructure', plus expanded early childhood education access (campaign issues)

candidates.name: Marty Jackley
candidates.background: South Dakota's Attorney General since 2023, who also held the office from 2009 to 2019 and served as U.S. Attorney for South Dakota from 2006 to 2009. He was raised in Sturgis, took an electrical engineering degree from the South Dakota School of Mines and a law degree from the University of South Dakota, and clerked for Chief Federal Judge Richard Battey. He owns a farm at Vale and a ranch near Pierre. He won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary over James Bialota by roughly 80 to 20 and is running for the open seat Rep. Dusty Johnson left to run for governor.
priorities: Border security and stopping drug trafficking
Cutting taxes and reducing the size of government

cost.label: On joining a multistate suit against California's packaging law: 'This is an unconstitutional mandate that will result in higher costs for businesses and ultimately higher prices for consumers', arguing the rules are 'unreasonable, burdensome requirements on businesses and consumers nationwide' (KOTA)

immigration.label: 'The meth and fentanyl on our streets come across an open border. I have prosecuted the traffickers who bring it here. Secure the border, finish the wall, and let law enforcement do its job' (campaign issues page)

taxes.label: Campaign commitment to 'strengthen our economy, secure our borders, rebuild our national defense, reduce the size of government, and cut taxes for hard working Americans' (campaign announcement page)

safety.label: 'I have spent my career putting violent criminals behind bars. In Congress I will back our police, sheriffs, and prosecutors with the tools and the respect they have earned. Public safety comes first' (campaign issues page)

repro.label: On defending South Dakota's abortion pill advertising law after a federal injunction: 'protecting and defending innocent life is and remains important to our Legislature, Governor, Attorney General and citizens' (KOTA)

democracy.label: Pressed the U.S. Senate to pass the SAVE America Act's proof of citizenship requirement: 'This is common-sense legislation to protect the integrity of our elections' (KOTA)

candidates.name: Nicole Gronli
candidates.now: President of Flatlander Strategies, a marketing company
candidates.background: Small business owner from rural Dell Rapids who led USDA Rural Development in South Dakota from 2022 to 2025, overseeing federal investments in rural housing, broadband, infrastructure and community facilities. She has nearly 30 years in marketing and communications, served on Dakota State University's cyber security industry advisory board and as president of the Department of Defense STARBASE board, and is a former vice chair of the South Dakota Democratic Party. She grew up in Aurora, South Dakota. She was unopposed for the Democratic nomination on June 2, 2026. News coverage generally calls her Nikki Gronli.

cost.label: Mixed: opposes broad tariffs and says of farmers 'never once have I been told by a farmer or a rancher that all they want is a bailout. They want markets', while also arguing government must protect the state's top industries because 'If our top industries in South Dakota are financially damaged, that trickles down to Main Street' (South Dakota Searchlight)

health.label: 'Congress should modernize Medicare's GME funding and expand rural and community-based training programs', 'Congress should make a major new investment in the NHSC', and 'As a member of Congress, I would not only sustain but increase our investment in proven programs' (campaign post on rural health care)

immigration.label: Platform bullet under Public Safety: 'Supporting eliminating ICE enforcement in South Dakota' (campaign priorities page)

taxes.label: 'Opposing federal tax breaks for data centers and ensuring companies pay for infrastructure, energy, and water' (campaign priorities page)

education.label: Would 'Fully fund IDEA so schools can provide students with disabilities proper education and services', 'Protect Title I funding for low-income family schools', 'Support competitive teacher pay and recruitment efforts in rural communities' and 'Invest in rural schools', and opposes closing the U.S. Department of Education (campaign priorities page)

safety.label: 'Nikki believes ensuring citizen safety is the way to guide and assist, not to harm, isolate, or discriminate'; names that 'Women in South Dakota are incarcerated at the highest rate in the WORLD' and backs 'Strengthening programs preventing domestic violence and sexual assault' (campaign priorities page)

repro.label: Says 'without bodily autonomy, your right to keep the Government out of the doctor's office becomes null'; backs keeping government out of personal medical decisions (campaign priorities page)

democracy.label: 'Supporting accommodations for in-person and mail-in voting' (campaign priorities page)
